To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the age of the stellar systems of radio galaxies, which are the oldest among elliptical galaxies, does not exceed 10 Gyr, and the age of the Universe is 13 Gyr.

the age of the stellar systems of elliptical galaxies is $t_0\sim 12$ Gyr and $t_0=11\pm1$ Gyr, the age of the Universe is $t_{Univ} \sim 14.2$ Gyr and the age of the stars in the Universe is $T_{Univ} =13\pm 1$ Gyr.

the age of the stellar systems of the elliptical galaxies is determined by the photometric data of the galaxies, the age of stellar systems of elliptical galaxies is in a range from 8 to 15 Gyrs and that the age of formation and evolution of stellar systems of galaxies is not related to the cosmological model of the Universe.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the determination of cosmological parameters $h$ and $\Omega_{\Lambda}$ from the data of photometry of elliptical galaxies.
the determination of the cosmology parameters from photometric data.
the determination of the age of stellar systems in the early Universe, and with an estimate of the cosmological parameter $\Omega_\Lambda$.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the value of the Hubble constant is $H_0\sim60$ km s$^{-1}$ Mpc$^{-1}$.
the cosmological parameters of the model PEGAE, $H_0$, $\Omega_\Lambda$, are consistent with those of the model GISSEL.
the cosmological parameters $\Omega_\Lambda =0.8 \pm 0.1$ and $H_00=72\pm 10$ km s$^{-1}$ Mpc$^{-1}$ are the best estimates of these parameters.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cosmological parameters $\Omega_\Lambda$, $H_0$, and $q_0$ can be determined by means of photometric observations of radio galaxies.
, in spite of the large scatter of data, the age-redshift dependence for elliptical galaxies is well defined.
the results are in good agreement with the data of other cosmological methods.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the age of the stellar systems in elliptical galaxies is a function of the redshift.
the age-redshift relation is not sensitive to the choice of the evolutionary synthesis model, and the cosmological parameters are determined in a consistent way.
the cosmological model with $\Omega_\Lambda\sim0.8$ is preferable to other cosmological models, in particular to models with $\Omega_\lambda\sim0.7$ and $\Lambda\sim0$.
